### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 were not observed in any of the 200 traces; in the later window they occur in about 30, 41 and 30 in 100 traces respectively (59, 82 and 60 of 200). [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- In the earlier window the segment ran as a tight chain: about 99 in 100 of A27's outgoing steps went to A28, about 99 in 100 of A28's outgoing steps went to A29, and A27 was followed by A29 exactly two steps later in about 99 in 100 cases. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG002]
- In the later window, A27 and A28 route a large share of their outgoing steps to the three previously unseen activities: A27 sends about 44 in 100 to A28 but about 22 to A20, 17 to A25 and 15 to A19; A28 still sends about 55 in 100 to A29 but about 42 combined to A20, A19 and A25. [DIR004, DIR005]
- The new activities lead mostly onward to A28 (about 52–56 in 100 of their outgoing steps) or directly to A29 (about 42–46 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- In the later window the three act as mutually exclusive alternatives: A19 and A20 never share a trace and the other pairs co-occur in at most about 1 in 200 traces, while each of them co-occurs with A27, with A28 and with A29 in essentially every trace in which it appears. [REL001, REL002, REL006, REL003, REL007, REL010]
- Their placement is consistent: they always follow A27 (A27 first in about 29–40 in 100 traces, the reverse essentially never) and always precede A29 (about 30–39 in 100, reverse essentially never), while around A28 both orders occur in similar proportions. [REL003, REL007, REL010, REL005, REL009, REL012, REL004, REL008, REL011]
- Step distances widened accordingly: A27→A28 adjacent fell from about 99 to about 44 in 100 (two steps apart in about 55 in 100), A28→A29 adjacent fell from about 99 to about 56 in 100, and A27→A29 moved from two steps apart (about 99 in 100) to three steps apart (about 97 in 100). [LAG001, LAG003, LAG002]
- A27 now occurs slightly earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.48 vs 0.46) and A29 slightly later (about 0.55 vs 0.57), each in all traces of both windows. [POS004, POS005]
- Minor: A10 participation rose from about 5 to about 13 in 100 traces (10 vs 27 of 200). [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, one of A19, A20 or A25 is executed as an optional step between A27 and A29 in roughly 30–41 in 100 traces, the three acting as mutually exclusive alternatives, whereas in the earlier window the flow passed directly from A27 via A28 to A29 and none of the three was observed. The placement is shown directly: each new activity co-occurs with A27, A28 and A29 in essentially all of its traces, always after A27 and before A29 [REL003, REL005, REL007, REL009, REL010, REL012]; A27 and A28 now route roughly 40–55 in 100 of their outgoing steps to these activities [DIR004, DIR005]; and the step distances between A27, A28 and A29 widened by exactly the amount expected if one extra step is inserted [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]. The slight position shifts of A27 (earlier) and A29 (later) are consistent with this [POS004, POS005]. Screening qualified 29 items where roughly 0.54 would be expected by chance for 109 tested units, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: the new step's order around A28 is mixed (each order in roughly 13–23 in 100 traces), so the evidence pins the insertion only to the segment between A27 and A29, not to a single point [REL004, REL008, REL011]. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A19, A20 and A25 already existed at rates too low to be sampled in 200 traces; even so, a rise to roughly a third of all traces is far beyond what sampling noise explains. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

Other differences: A10 was observed in about 5 in 100 traces before and about 13 in 100 after (10 vs 27 of 200), a modest rise resting on few observations. [OCC001]
